chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Aslam from a man from the people of Al-Jazirah who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): A group of people were shipwrecked in the sea, so they went out walking along the shore, and they found a dead man naked. The people had nothing on them except handkerchiefs which they wrapped around themselves, and they did not have an excess garment to cover the man. So how should they pray over him while he is naked? He said: 'If they cannot find a garment to cover his private parts, let them dig his grave and place him in his grave (lahd), covering his private parts with bricks or stones or with earth. Then they should pray over him, and then cover him in his grave.' I said: 'And do they not pray over him after he has been buried?' He said: 'No. If that were permissible for anyone, it would be permissible for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Therefore, prayer is not performed over the buried, nor over the naked.'

key_terms.لَحْدِهِ: his grave (specifically the niche in the side of the grave)

ai.seo_question: How to perform funeral prayer over a naked corpse without clothing?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the procedural sequence for funeral prayer when covering the *awrah* of a naked corpse is challenging, such as after a shipwreck. He establishes that if no garment is available, the private parts may be covered with earth, stones, or bricks within the grave, and the prayer is performed prior to burial. Crucially, he rules out praying over the already buried or the naked corpse in situ, citing the precedent of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to affirm that the prayer must precede interment.
